questions.q: What is the real Terraform provider source used to manage Snowflake account objects?
options: azure/snowflake
hashicorp/snowflake
snowflake/terraform-provider
Snowflake-Labs/snowflake
questions.explain: Snowflake-Labs/snowflake is the real, current Terraform provider source for Snowflake resources.

questions.q: Why do DRIFTWOOD_ETL_WH and DRIFTWOOD_BI_WH have different auto_suspend values?
options: auto_suspend values must always increase for each warehouse defined after the first
This is an arbitrary difference with no real reasoning behind it
They're genuinely different workloads -- the ETL warehouse runs in a tight daily burst and should suspend fast, while the BI warehouse serves sporadic queries and benefits from staying warm longer
Terraform requires every warehouse resource to have a unique auto_suspend value
questions.explain: The different values reflect each warehouse's actual usage pattern -- the same workload-aware reasoning applied to the warehouse split in Lesson 2.

questions.q: What does Terraform provision in this capstone, and what does it deliberately never touch?
options: It replaces the need for Airflow entirely
It only manages Power BI dashboards, not Snowflake objects
It provisions both infrastructure and runs all dbt transformations
It provisions infrastructure (databases, warehouses, roles, grants); it never provisions the actual subscriber data or runs dbt models
questions.explain: The line between infrastructure and data is deliberate and consistent with how the Terraform & Bicep course treats its own Azure resources.

questions.q: Where is data_retention_time_in_days set for the DRIFTWOOD_ANALYTICS database, and why does that matter?
options: It defaults to a value Terraform cannot override
In the Terraform resource definition itself, so it's provisioned as part of the database's definition from day one, not configured by hand later and possibly forgotten
It cannot be set via Terraform and must be configured separately
It's set manually in the Snowflake console after the database is created
questions.explain: Setting it in code from the start avoids relying on someone remembering to configure it by hand afterward -- a real, named benefit of infrastructure as code.

questions.q: What happens when a pull request changes a .tf file, versus when that PR is merged to main?
options: Nothing runs automatically at either stage -- all Terraform commands are run manually
A PR runs terraform plan (a reviewable diff); only a merge to main runs terraform apply
Both plan and apply run automatically on every PR, before any review
terraform apply runs on the PR, and terraform plan runs only after merge
questions.explain: Plan-on-PR, apply-on-merge is the same discipline taught in the Terraform & Bicep course -- proposed changes are reviewable before they take effect.
